beats.intent: The viewer understands that ThinkSR connects compact thought representations to dense super-resolution output.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: ThinkSR starts from a mismatch between how CTM represents thought and what super-resolution must produce.

params.headline: Compact thought must serve dense output
params.sub: A dense carrier lets a compact process update a spatial field.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that the central problem is a representation mismatch between compact CTM state and spatially dense reconstruction.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: The compact side is useful for thought-like computation. The dense side is required because every output location needs spatial detail. The method has to connect these two forms without losing the field.

params.headline: CTM is compact, but super-resolution is spatially dense
params.note: The method must bridge the two representations.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that DQ-CTM is presented as a comparison point alongside CTM and a window-wise adaptation.
beats.claim: CTM, a window-wise adaptation, and DQ-CTM compared.
beats.narration: The comparison establishes three versions of the idea. The original CTM is the compact reference. The window-wise adaptation adds spatial partitioning. DQ-CTM is the version used for super-resolution.

params.headline: DQ-CTM is compared with CTM and a window-wise variant

beats.intent: The viewer understands that ThinkSR keeps a persistent dense carrier, while a compact thought process reads and updates it.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method keeps the dense field present throughout the computation. The compact process reads from that carrier. The same process updates the carrier again, so spatial detail remains available.

params.headline: A dense carrier persists while compact thought updates it
params.note: The carrier is not replaced by the compact state.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that the dense carrier is encoded from the low-resolution input and partitioned into windows.
beats.narration: The low-resolution image first becomes a feature field. The encoder creates the dense carrier. Windowing turns that carrier into the working inputs. The windows keep the computation tied to the spatial field.

params.headline: The carrier is encoded first, then windowed

beats.intent: The viewer understands that ThinkSR runs end to end through encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, and decoder.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The end-to-end path starts by encoding the low-resolution image. The encoded field is split into windows. Shared DQ-CTM ticks process those windows. The decoder turns the processed field into the reconstruction.

params.headline: ThinkSR flows from encoder to windows to shared ticks to decoder
params.note: The stages match the end-to-end diagram.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that windowing is the spatial structure inside the ThinkSR path.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: Windowing gives the dense carrier a local structure. Each lit region is part of the same carrier. The partition is the bridge from field data into window-level processing.

params.headline: The carrier is partitioned into window inputs
params.note: The equation names this operation as windowing over the carrier.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that the reconstruction is shown across ticks from T=0 through T=4, compared with bicubic and ground truth.
beats.claim: Reconstruction at T=0 through T=4 against bicubic and ground truth.
beats.narration: The reconstruction is tracked across successive ticks. The starting point is compared with bicubic. Later ticks show the same crop as the process continues. Ground truth anchors the comparison.

params.headline: Reconstruction is shown from T=0 through T=4

beats.intent: The viewer understands that the error maps use the same crops and one shared colour scale.
beats.claim: Absolute-error maps on the same crops, one shared colour scale.
beats.narration: The error maps compare absolute error on the same crops. A shared colour scale keeps the maps comparable. That makes differences in error intensity meaningful across methods.

params.headline: Absolute error is compared on one shared colour scale

beats.intent: The viewer understands that DQ-CTM-SR is competitive with CNN baselines but trails the recent lightweight transformer CATANet.
beats.claim: Competitive with CNN baselines; behind recent lightweight transformers.
beats.narration: The benchmark reports parameters and average score together. DQ-CTM-SR is close to the CNN baselines in average score. CATANet has the highest reported average. DQ-CTM-SR uses more parameters than the listed lightweight transformer.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is competitive with CNNs but behind CATANet
params.note: Average is over five benchmarks for x4 lightweight super-resolution.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that DQ-CTM-SR has more parameters than IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet in the reported table, but fewer than CARN.
beats.narration: Parameter count shows a different tradeoff than score. CARN is the largest listed model. DQ-CTM-SR is smaller than CARN. It is larger than IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR sits between CARN and smaller baselines in size
params.note: Values are the reported parameter counts.

beats.intent: The viewer understands that DQ-CTM-SR's average score is near CARN, IMDN, and RFDN, while CATANet is higher.
beats.narration: Average score is tightly grouped for the CNN baselines and DQ-CTM-SR. RFDN reports a slightly higher average than DQ-CTM-SR. CATANet is the clear leader in this table. That is the stated gap to recent lightweight transformers.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is close to CNN baselines and below CATANet
params.note: Average is reported over five benchmarks.
